answer: A museum hires agents to inspect each relic for damage. A camera moves along a trellis of fixed viewpoints, while a whisper alert carries only a hash of a suspected crack until the inspection window closes. The museum pays one bounty per verified crack, shared among all matching reports, and requires a refundable deposit for each distinct claim. An attacker running many identities must find new real defects and lock more capital; copied reports merely split the same bounty. Camera tampering and collusion remain possible, so curators compare independent images and audit disputed claims.
